We need to answer based on policy excerpts. The customer says "Suspect a payload size limit is quietly cutting off data." Likely they are asking about webhook payload size limit and how to handle truncated data. The policy says payload is capped, large records delivered as reference with truncated:true flag, need to fetch full record via API. Also suggests subscribing to .changed event and fetching full record to avoid size cap. Also says batching not configurable.

Thus answer: explain that payload size is capped, large records are sent as reference with truncated flag, you should detect that flag and fetch full record via API; for frequent large records use .changed event and fetch by id; cannot change batching.

Provide short answer.

function.arguments: {"message":"Hi there – Meridian webhooks have a fixed payload size limit. When a record’s full content would exceed that limit, the webhook sends only a reference (the record ID) with a `truncated: true` flag instead of a partial payload. Your integration should watch for that flag and then retrieve the complete record via the API using the provided ID. If you regularly get large records, consider subscribing to the `.changed` event and always fetching the current record by ID rather than relying on the webhook payload; this bypasses the size cap entirely. Note that webhook batching isn’t configurable – each change is delivered as its own event, so any batching must be handled on your side after you fetch the records."}

arguments.message: Hi there – Meridian webhooks have a fixed payload size limit. When a record’s full content would exceed that limit, the webhook sends only a reference (the record ID) with a `truncated: true` flag instead of a partial payload. Your integration should watch for that flag and then retrieve the complete record via the API using the provided ID. If you regularly get large records, consider subscribing to the `.changed` event and always fetching the current record by ID rather than relying on the webhook payload; this bypasses the size cap entirely. Note that webhook batching isn’t configurable – each change is delivered as its own event, so any batching must be handled on your side after you fetch the records.
